title: Adam and Eve as a memory of genetic manipulation

tellings.quote: >> when uh they talk about the first human beings I assume that that is a recounting of a genetic manipulation.
So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;
And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

plain: The claim is that the Bible's story of the first humans, Adam and Eve, is a memory of genetic manipulation, with humans made by changing beings that already existed. The comedian and interviewer Joe Rogan offers this to Michels as his own reading: when old texts 'talk about the first human beings I assume that that is a recounting of a genetic manipulation.' He points to the King James Bible of 1611. Its Book of Genesis, traditionally credited to Moses, says 'God created man in his own image' and that 'the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.' It also says God 'caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam,' took one of his ribs, and from it 'made he a woman.' The text tells of the first humans being made by a higher hand. Reading that making as genetic work done on beings already alive is Rogan's step, which the text neither states nor excludes. If true, the Genesis story would be an old record of humans being engineered by someone else.

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: In the King James Version, Genesis tells that God "created man in his own image", that "the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life", and that he made the woman from a rib he took from Adam during "a deep sleep", a making of the first humans by a higher hand. Reading that making as genetic work done on beings already living is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.
